hints: Look at the first cross result. Black x splashed-white gives all blue, an intermediate phenotype. What does that tell you about dominance between $C^B$ and $C^S$?
Look at where the second gene is located. It is on the Z chromosome but not on the W chromosome. What name is given to inheritance of genes carried on sex chromosomes?
walkthrough:
Why Feather Colour Is Not Simple Dominance**
Black crossed with splashed-white does not give black or white, it gives a third, intermediate phenotype - blue - in all offspring. That means in the heterozygote $C^BC^S$ both alleles have an effect and neither masks the other. That is codominance.

Why Feather Pattern Is Sex-Linked**
The pattern gene is carried on the Z chromosome and has no counterpart on the W chromosome. Any gene located on a sex chromosome shows sex-linked inheritance. In chickens males are $ZZ$ and females are $WZ$, the reverse of humans, but the principle is the same.
Final answer: feather colour: codominance; feather pattern: sex linkage.

hints: Start with feather colour, which is autosomal. If black and splashed-white parents always breed true, what must their $C$ genotypes be?
Now add the sex chromosomes. A male has two Z chromosomes, a female has Z and W. Write those empty frames first before adding A/a alleles.
Use the offspring pattern to work out A/a. All sons are barred but all daughters are non-barred. Which parent must have supplied the $Z^A$ allele to the sons?
Check what gametes each parent can make. Remember colour and pattern genes are on different chromosomes so they assort independently into the gamete.
Combine one gamete from each parent to make a son ($ZZ$) and a daughter ($WZ$). Check both get $C^BC^S$ for blue feathers.
walkthrough:
Work Out The Parental Colour Genotypes**
Black is $C^BC^B$ and splashed-white is $C^SC^S$. Both are homozygous because they breed true. That is why all offspring receive one $C^B$ and one $C^S$ and are heterozygous $C^BC^S$ with blue feathers.

Work Out The Parental Pattern Genotypes**
Males are $ZZ$, females are $WZ$. The non-barred black male must be $Z^aZ^a$ because he shows the recessive trait and has two copies. The barred splashed-white female must be $WZ^A$ because she has only one Z chromosome, so her single allele determines her phenotype. So full genotypes are male $C^BC^BZ^aZ^a$ and female $C^SC^SWZ^A$.

Write The Gametes**
The male can only make one type of gamete for these genes: $C^BZ^a$. The female makes two types: $C^SZ^A$ going to sons and $C^SW$ going to daughters, because sons receive Z from mother and daughters receive W from mother.

Combine To Get Offspring**
$C^BZ^a$ + $C^SZ^A$ gives $C^BC^SZ^AZ^a$, a $ZZ$ male that is blue and barred because $Z^A$ is dominant. $C^BZ^a$ + $C^SW$ gives $C^BC^SWZ^a$, a $WZ$ female that is blue and non-barred because she has only $Z^a$. This matches the observed 1:1 sex-specific pattern.

Final answer: parents genotype: male $C^BC^BZ^aZ^a$ x female $C^SC^SWZ^A$; gametes: $C^BZ^a$ x $C^SZ^A$ and $C^SW$; offspring genotypes: male $C^BC^SZ^AZ^a$, female $C^BC^SWZ^a$; phenotypes: male blue barred, female blue non-barred.

hints: A blue barred male must be $C^BC^S$ for colour, so colour is already known. Which part of his genotype is still uncertain - $Z^AZ^A$ or $Z^AZ^a$?
Recall the standard cross used to find out if a dominant phenotype is hiding a recessive allele. What type of partner with a fully recessive phenotype would you choose?
Think about what daughters get from their father. If the male gives $Z^A$ to every daughter, what will you see, and what if he gives $Z^a$ to half his daughters?
walkthrough:
Identify What Is Unknown**
Any blue bird must be $C^BC^S$, so colour genotype is certain. The problem is the barred pattern. A barred male could be homozygous dominant $Z^AZ^A$ or heterozygous $Z^AZ^a$, and both look barred because A is dominant.

Choose A Test Cross Partner**
Cross him to a non-barred female, genotype $WZ^a$. She is hemizygous recessive and can only pass $Z^a$ to sons and W to daughters, so any $Z^a$ appearing in barred sons or any non-barred daughters must have come from the male being tested.

Interpret The Offspring**
If the male is $Z^AZ^A$, he gives $Z^A$ to all children, so all sons and all daughters will be barred. If the male is $Z^AZ^a$, about half his sons get $Z^a$ and half his daughters get $Z^a$ (showing as non-barred because females have only one Z), so the appearance of any non-barred offspring proves he is heterozygous.

Final answer: Blue is heterozygous $C^BC^S$ so only barred locus needs testing; carry out a test cross to a non-barred female ($WZ^a$); if all offspring barred, male is $Z^AZ^A$, if any non-barred offspring appear, male is $Z^AZ^a$.
